odia: ଜାଣିଥିଲିକି? କିଏ ସୂନା କିଏ ପିତଳ ବୋଲି ନିକିତି ପକେଇ ତୁଳି ଥିଲିକି?
title: Had I weighed them?
literal_meaning: Did I know? Had I put them on a balance and weighed who was gold and who was brass?
explanation: Two questions resist the expectation of prior knowledge. Gold and brass give the contrast a material image, while the balance suggests examination. Our reading hears someone explaining a mistaken judgment: they had not tested what they were asked to recognise. The source supplies no particular deception, person or transaction.
meaning_odia: ଦୁଇଟି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିଥିବାର ଆଶାକୁ ଅଟକାଏ। ସୁନା ଓ ପିତଳ ବିରୋଧକୁ ବସ୍ତୁର ଛବି ଦିଏ, ନିକିତି ପରଖିବାକୁ ମନେ ପକାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଭୁଲ ବିଚାରର ସଫେଇ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ—ଯାହାକୁ ଚିହ୍ନିବା ଆଶା କରାଗଲା, ତାକୁ ପରଖାଯାଇନଥିଲା। ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଠକାମି, ମଣିଷ ବା କାରବାର ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading hears a defence against being expected to know without examining.
odia_summary: ନ ପରଖି ଜାଣିବାର ଆଶା ବିରୋଧରେ ଆମ ପଢ଼ାର ସଫେଇ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ଶୁଣିଥିବା ଖବର ଆଗକୁ କହିଦେଲେ; ପରେ ତାହା ଭୁଲ ବୋଲି ଜଣାଗଲା। ସେ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ଆଗରୁ ପରଖିନଥିଲି; ଏବେ ସଂଶୋଧନଟି ମଧ୍ୟ ଜଣାଇବି।” / Someone passes on a report that proves false. Recalling the saying, they admit, “I had not checked it; now I will pass on the correction too.” This response is invented.
cultural_context: The balance is a source image, not evidence that weighing alone identifies metal composition. The interpretation establishes no hierarchy of human worth.
